First, some background.

So I'm a mid twenties male who is pretty skinny (low muscle mass) and am starting to get leaner. I was skinny growing up and had a BMI that was in the underweight regime (18). I never did anything physical growing up. I was a complete nerd and stayed away from anything sports related - I was basically anti-interested in physical activity. After college though, my BMI was now in the "healthy" regime (21ish). However, my physical habits were the same. I noticed a bit of a pudge and a bit of a muffin top starting. I was becoming what I later learned was a skinny fat....

This was before I even knew about fph.. and I was disgusted with myself. I was completely disgusted with the idea of becoming some fat blob. I knew I had to change something then while it was still super easy. I began working out regularly and watching what I ate. Gasp! What a crazy idea!!!! A year later, I'm the same BMI and I have no pudge or even the slightest hint of a muffin top.

Fast forward to today. I really had begun wishing I kept track of my weight and resting heart rate the entire time I began working out because I would love to track my progress. Along with that, I thought it would be cool to know my body fat.

Today I had an appointment with my doctor (who is a human, fortunately) about something unrelated. At the end of it, I asked him if he knew where I could get a good body fat measurement.

"But why?!" He exclaimed. "You're so skinny! " "Because I'm really interested in getting data on myself so I can check my progress," I explained.

He seemed really skeptical about my reasons and thought I was obsessed with my weight and insinuated, somewhat jokingly, that I was anorexic, which really really upset me.

"Can an anorexic run a six minute mile?" I asked him. "An anorexic would snap in two trying to run at any kind of speed!"

He didn't really have a response to that.

I asked him if he would be this concerned about a patent asking for a body fat measurement if his patient was obese. He said, "of course not," in a "well-duh" kind of tone. In the end he did direct me to people that could help me get some more info about my body. I'm pretty interested in getting my VO2 max checked too....

I never thought I'd get thinned shamed by a doctor....
I think I was thin shamed?

it doesn't sound like you were thin shamed, honestly. it may have been awkward, but if anything doctors tend to overlook eating disorders in men, so i think it was good medicine for him to approach the subject with you. asking for clarification when an already-very-thin patient seems preoccupied with body fat isn't thin shaming. i do think he could've approached it better, though, if you felt bad afterward!

Absolutely. It'd irresponsible and unprofessional for a doctor not to ask why when a patient requests a certain type of treatment or examination. He might even have had actual anorexics come in and ask for the same thing before.

If anything, it sounds like he's taking your mental health into consideration. If someone who's healthy and skinny comes in asking how to lose weight or questions similar to that nature, chances are they're looking to get into an unhealthy weight. You're at 21ish BMI, and that's in the healthy range. 18 is underweight. If you claimed you were 18 bmi, and now you're 21 bmi and you're interested in stuff like this, the doctor is probably looking out for you, the same way he'd look out for you if you were 24 bmi last time and came in for a checkup at 26 bmi.

My assumption is he's seen enough people that are in the low but still healthy bmi ranges, that are trying to get down into the underweight bmi ranges and it's more common than someone just interested in finding out their body fat.
